Use case: illustration-story. Asset: ONE original 4:5 vertical everyday-life scene keyframe for Mochi & Lucky, no finished typography.
Reference image 1 is the accepted blue-studio keyframe: strictly preserve Mochi's original fluffy orange-gold kitten, cream muzzle/chest, pink nose and round warm dark eyes; Lucky's warm charcoal BLACK shorter-furred kitten, large pointed ears, small dark nose and yellow-green round eyes. Reference image 2 is the original painting and defines LARGE flat broken matte gouache brush masses and simplified natural kitten proportions. These are our original cats, not upright human mascots. No fine individual-hair rendering, polished shading, airbrush, vector outlines, clothing, human hands, human grins, permanent accessories, or copied franchise characters. Keep connected cat anatomy, consistent small cat mouths and recognizable face/ear/head-body proportions.
Setting: a tiny reading nook with a LOW bookcase, books with blank spines, a cream floor cushion and one very clear rectangular patch of afternoon sunlight on the painted blue floor.
Acting and staging: Mochi LEFT is naturally loafed in the warm rectangle, eyes almost closed; Lucky RIGHT sits just outside the warm patch, politely inspecting the tiny remaining corner as if asking for a reservation. Mochi has subtly shifted so one small warm corner remains available for Lucky. Both kittens anatomically complete, no book held like a human; the light is a flat painted warm shape, not digital glow.
Paint the cats and environment together as one coherent chunky gouache illustration, NOT separate stickers on a beige layout. Clear cat-eye-level staging, understated deadpan warmth, recognizable natural kitten silhouettes. Cats prominent, all ears and visible paws comfortably inside; any body occlusion comes only from real scene props, not detached anatomy. Keep enough of the location visible to make this scene distinctly different from a studio desk. Warm orange/cream with painterly blue and restrained location accents. Matte grouped color planes, not airbrushed gradients, glows or finely rendered hairs.
No laptop, computer, product interface, brand logo, sales message, written text, numbers, speech bubbles, title, labels, border or watermark. No humanoid standing torso, hand gestures, costumes, broad grins, slapstick violence, rooftop edges or hazardous staging. Avoid copying the original diagonal overhead composition or repeating the same seated-two-cats-in-front-of-a-table arrangement. New scenes are proposals, not permanent approved canon.
